#1294. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. Odegaard with a poor pass in the middle of the park, but Konsa produced a tremendous block to stop Kane’s left-footed shot across Raya.

Calafiori was super advanced within the first 30 seconds, straight into an attacking midfield zone. Davies is indeed playing as a left-winger for Bayern in front of Stanisic. In the very early exchanges, Bayern are enjoying more of the ball, but the game still to settle into a pattern.

Arsenal get the game under way, playing in their navy away kit.

It seems like Vincent Kompany may have taken a leaf out of Thomas Tuchel’s tactical book. When Arsenal came here in 2024, Tuchel deployed two left-backs on that flank (Mazraoui and Guerreiro) after saying in the press conference that Arsenal’s right-sided attackers were the danger. Kompany appears to have done the same here with Davies, usually a left-back, starting as a winger.

Kane has already played against Arsenal since leaving Spurs, so some of the vinegar has gone out of that sub-plot but it is still worth noting that he has scored 15 goals in 22 appearances against them. Several of those goals have been penalties, but Kane is so much more than a goalscorer these days, especially at Bayern where at times he appears to have a free role.

A fascinating aspect of tonight’s game is how Konsa and Gabriel decide to deal with him. Will Arsenal commit to a man-to-man press, with the centre-backs following Kane well beyond the halfway line, or preserve a more zonal approach?

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Will the substitutes again make the difference for Arsenal tonight? In each of their last three league victories, they have won because of goals scored by substitutes. This speaks to the quality of Arteta’s squad, obviously, but also to the Arsenal manager’s ability to pick the right players for the right moments. Over the last year or so, this has become a real strength.

Karl had been expected to replace Olise on the right, but Kompany looks to have stiffened up his midfield by starting Pavlovic, Laimer and Bischof. It will be interesting to see how Saibari and Kane dovetail, two stick-on strikers. It is not Bayern’s strongest team, with Luis Diaz also on the bench.

Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Madueke

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Newcastle United and Brentford are reportedly keeping a close eye on Sporting CP midfielder Issa Doumbia, with several European clubs interested in signing him ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

According to a report from Fussball News, Napoli, Juventus and AS Roma are also monitoring the 23-year-old Italian midfielder, who has made a strong impression since arriving in Portugal from Venezia during the summer transfer window.

Napoli have already taken steps to explore a potential deal, having contacted people close to the player to gather information about his situation. The Serie A outfit are understood to be considering an approach in January, although competition for his signature could complicate their pursuit.

Newcastle and Brentford are also among the clubs following Doumbia’s development at Sporting. Both Premier League sides are understood to be impressed by his physical qualities and versatility, and his performances have attracted attention across Europe.

The midfielder could be an interesting addition for Newcastle, who would benefit from greater depth and physicality in the middle of the park. It is believed that bids in the region of €55–65 million could provide a starting point for discussions, although there is no guarantee that Sporting would agree to lower their demands.

#1292. Mauricio Pochettino leaves behind a negligible legacy at USMNT... where raised standards never materialized into results as tearful Argentine bolts for Man United

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino said when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

So now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

But Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

But he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

The results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

All the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have said in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

But it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success

The Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'

But not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling

All of this being said, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

It never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

#1291. Report Bruno Fernandes targeted by Milan along with Goncalo Inacio

Milan are reportedly pushing for more Portuguese players to join Ruben Amorim’s side, including Sporting defender Goncalo Inacio and Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes.

The Rossoneri have had a definite Portuguese flavour in recent years, already going through coaches Sergio Conceicao and Paulo Fonseca, then hiring Amorim over the summer.

They brought in striker Goncalo Ramos as their most expensive ever signing, and while Diego Moreira plays his international football for Belgium, he was a Portugal player at youth level.

It was no secret that Milan had pursued Sporting CP defender Goncalo Inacio over the summer, and they are widely expected to try again in the January transfer window.

It won’t be easy, as the asking price is a minimum of €40m, because his contract runs to June 2030 and has a release clause worth €60m.

According to The Athletic, another Portuguese name on their radar is Bruno Fernandes, who is frustrated at Manchester United and the arrival of new coach Mauricio Pochettino might not revitalise his fortunes.

Juventus have already been linked with the former Sampdoria and Novara midfielder, whose contract runs to June 2027 with an option to extend.

Milan are now also showing an interest in his situation, hoping for a low-cost option adding more experience to the midfield that already has Luka Modric.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

Published: 16:25 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:42 EST, 14 November 2026

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

#1287. Nations League official line-ups: Belgium vs. Italy

Italy bring Luca Koleosho and Niccolò Pisilli into a trident with Pio Esposito, as they battle for the Nations League quarter-final spot against Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere’s Belgium.

It kicks off at the King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens on the Liveblog.

The Azzurri started this Roberto Mancini era on September 25 with a 2-0 home defeat to Belgium, but have gone from strength to strength with victories over Turkiye, a 1-1 draw in Paris, and Thursday’s remarkable 3-1 comeback win over France at San Siro.

Pio Esposito scored twice in that game and leads the attack again here, but his brother Sebastiano has been left behind, while Davide Frattesi and Nicolò Cambiaghi have both pulled out through injury.

Nicolò Fagioli is brought into midfield to replace injured Frattesi, while the rest of the team stays intact from Thursday.

A point would suffice for Italy to qualify for the quarter-finals, but a win would secure top spot ahead of France thanks to the superior head-to-head record.

Belgium are in third place because of their two narrow defeats to France, but sit only one point behind their rivals.

Former Napoli striker Romelu Lukaku missed the 2-1 comeback win over Turkiye and is therefore only on the bench today, so Atalanta striker De Ketelaere again leads the line as a False 9.

#1286. He Played With Jamie Carragher and Emile Heskey, But is Now in Jail After £15m Scam

Sadly, there are many examples of talented footballers who end up in prison. Success in football is no guarantee, but even those who make it at a high level don't always stay on the right path.

El-Hadji Diouf, Joey Barton and Duncan Ferguson are just some of the ex-Premier League stars who ended up behind bars for various reasons. Even past Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho spent time in prison after using a fake passport back in March 2020 – former Barcelona teammate Lionel Messi supposedly helped bail the Brazilian out.

Richard Rufus is a lesser-known footballer who was sent to prison and remains in jail to this day.

For a number of years, Richard Rufus was a mainstay in the Charlton Athletic defence. He came through the club's youth system and was just 19 when he made his debut in 1994. One season later, he was named in the PFA Team of the Year for the Football League First Division (now Championship).

The talented centre-back was also capped for England at the U21 level, sharing game time with future Three Lions senior stars such as Emile Heskey and Jamie Carragher. Rufus, though, never got a first-team call-up, and spent his entire career with Charlton.

He won promotion to the Premier League on two occasions under Alan Curbishley. With a total of 254 games for the Addicks, the Englishman was even voted by fans as the club's greatest defender in 2005, just one year after he retired.

In the years since hanging up his boots, however, Rufus has unfortunately taken a dark path away from football and into crime.

While Olise was attending the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, his old teammate was in court.

In December 2013, Rufus was declared bankrupt after a £6m failed investment, which cost his church £5m. But the issues did not stop there.

Just two years later, he was branded a 'fraudster' by a specialist civil court judge following an £8m loss to investors relating to a Ponzi scheme. Then in 2023, a press release from the City of London Police confirmed that the former footballer had been jailed for over seven years for his £15m investment scam:

"A former footballer who convinced up to 100 friends and members of his family to invest a total of more than £15 million in a foreign currency exchange scheme has been jailed for seven and a half years."

Rufus was found guilty of four counts of fraud by false representation, money laundering and one count of carrying out a regulated activity without authorisation. Detective Constable Claire Sandford-Day, from the fraud operations team at the City of London Police, said:

“Rufus deliberately deceived those who were close to him and those who trusted him to scam them out of substantial sums of money.

“He used his status as a former footballer to make it appear that he was leading a life of wealth as a result of his former career and investments, when the reality was, he was not making profits from his trading activities and was using the money from his victims to pay for his lifestyle.”

It was said that of the £15m paid to accounts controlled by Rufus, investors received back a total of around just £7.6 million. He was found to have used the money to fund his own lifestyle, spending almost £300,000 on shopping, car finance, travel and restaurants

As a result of the scam, friendships and loyalties between friends were said to be 'shattered', with many suffering from huge financial and mental health difficulties as a result of the scheme.

#1285. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

🗣️ Commitment. Resilience. Teamwork. Michael's powerful message in full 👇 https://t.co/vWwJt1fW47

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

"I think it's the feeling of entitlement that we have in our club" Ruben Amorim says some of the players at Manchester United may need a bit of a reality check 🎙️ https://t.co/PiJWML3TeH

In truth, so many of the post-Ferguson managers have spoken in similar ways – certainly Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho and Ralf Rangnick.

Listening to Carrick repeatedly talking about the need for humility, hard work, pride, sacrifice and resilience was a reminder of how the values that were once taken for granted at this football club have steadily been eroded.

Wayne Rooney said this week that United’s players were “selfish” and “babies”. Many top players over the years have been selfish but it helped drive them and, in turn, their team to great heights, but the same cannot be said about the current bunch.

Carrick spoke about trying to rediscover something that is “lost” at the moment. Whether they can is a big if. Opponents aside, the only winners at the moment from United’s latest crisis are Amazon.

#1284. Ronaldinho’s return: Best moments and key stats from the Brazilian legend’s game in Ravenna

Brazilian legend Ronaldinho came back from retirement on Sunday, playing 45 minutes for Ravenna in a Serie C match against Forlì, where he made 28 touches and helped score his side’s opening goal.

It was a historic day for Ravenna, as the local side, playing in Italy’s third division, Serie C, saw Brazilian legend Ronaldinho return to action wearing their shirt.

Football Italia was among the accredited media at the Stadio Benelli.

The 12,000-seat stadium sold out despite protests over high prices and the blocking of season ticket holders, who still had to buy tickets for the game despite their presale rights.

Ronaldinho’s return to action, more than ten years after his last competitive appearance, was part of a wider partnership with Ravenna President Ignazio Cipriani.

Ravenna formally signed Ronaldinho this past June, when the ex-Milan and Barcelona star also became a brand ambassador for the Emilia-Romagna-based club and a minority shareholder.

His deal with Ravenna was announced at an event in Miami this past June, during the 2026 World Cup.

As expected, the legendary No.10 started today’s game against local rivals Forlì. The gap between the two teams was considerable coming into the game: Ravenna are fighting for promotion to Serie B, sitting second, while Forlì sit 15th and hope to avoid finishing in a relegation play-off place.

28 Touches 1 Key pass 81% Passing accuracy

It’s crazy I’m writing this 😂 https://t.co/CPGwSjKEiB

— Lorenzo Bettoni (@LoreBetto) November 15, 2026

Ronaldinho, 46, was the most advanced Ravenna player when the home side was forced to track back to defend, but operated as an attacking midfielder in possession.

He made his first touch around five minutes in, taking a right-sided corner kick. His cross was pushed out of the box by the Forlì defence.

Overall, Ronaldinho made 28 touches, including one key pass. His second corner kick, also taken from the right, found a teammate inside the box and forced Forlì goalkeeper Luca Martelli to a diving save.

Every time Ronaldinho had the ball, the fans—including those in the away end—held their breath. Defenders weren’t too aggressive, except when, around the 30th minute, Luigi Palomba pounced on a dead ball and pushed the Brazilian with his shoulder. The home crowd briefly protested, and Ronaldinho did the same a few seconds later when he asked for a handball, claiming it had blocked his through ball.

At minute 35, Ronaldinho was involved in Ravenna’s opening goal, scored by ex-Monza and Inter defender Giulio Donati. The Brazilian received the ball through the middle and passed it to Lorenzo Lonardi, who assisted Donati for the opening goal.

Ronaldinho joined his teammates in celebration and played out the remaining ten minutes of the first half.

At the half-time whistle, both teams headed to the dressing rooms, but Ronaldinho remained on the pitch with fellow Brazilians and former Milan players Dida and Serginho.

He spent several minutes waving to supporters in the curva and the stands as they applauded him.

Having trained with his Ravenna teammates just once, on the eve of the match, Ronaldinho left the stadium during the second half. The hosts added another goal to seal a 2-0 win over their local rivals.

“It went by too fast; that has always been football for me,” the Brazilian told Sky Sports at half-time.

!Is this my last one? I don’t know, if the President keeps calling me, I will come back! It is always a pleasure. I told the President, if he needs me, then I will be here.”

#1283. Arsenal Scout £66m Vinicius Jr Alternative, Transfer Talks Underway

Arsenal are stepping up their pursuit of signing RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa ahead of the January transfer window, with scouts attending his last three matches.

According to TEAMTalk, the Gunners are interested and talks have started with Nusa’s representatives. But Leipzig are determined to keep the Norway international and value him at £66million. That figure would make him the club’s third most expensive signing of all-time, behind Declan Rice and the summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

A move to the Premier League champions is thought to appeal to Nusa, who is considered as an alternative to Vinicius Jr after he turned them down to remain at Real Madrid. As well as Arsenal, Bayern Munich are among the others keen on landing Nusa.

The 21-year-old has been in blistering form so far this season, scoring six goals and providing eight assists in 15 appearances for Leipzig.He found the net and impressed in Leipzig’s 3-2 defeat to Manchester City in the Champions League earlier this month, giving Matheus Nunes a real torrid time on that side.

Nusa has since taken his form into the November international break, as he produced a sensational performance during Norway’s 3-1 win against Wales on Saturday.He scored Norway’s opener on the hour mark, picking up a loose ball on the edge of the box before firing a low shot into the bottom corner, giving Karl Darlow no chance.

As well as that, Nusa had the most shots (4), the most touches in the opposition box (8) and recorded a 87 per cent pass accuracy. From a defensive point-of-view, Nusa did the hard yards, making three tackles, three interceptions and won six ground duels.He was awarded a 8/10 rating byTipsbladet, who hailed the Leipzig winger for 'doing everything on his own' and being a 'constant moment of unrest' for Welsh defenders.

Arsenal should sign Nusa in January. Although Christos Tzolis has made a fine start to life at the Emirates Stadium, it does feel as though the Gunners are still a top-class left-winger short of becoming a dominant force for years to come.

They tried to bring Vinicius to north London in the summer, only to be rejected by the Brazilian, who instead opted to commit his future to Real Madrid. And with Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard leaving for pastures new, it has left the Gunners light on that side. Eberechi Eze has filled in as back-up to Tzolis, who joined in a £34m deal from Club Brugge, and has done a decent job, but the left wing is no doubt their weakest area.

It would leave a gaping hole for Nusa to come in and be the nailed on starter in Mikel Arteta’s first XI at the Emirates. Right now, there aren't too many wingers better than Nusa in European football, and he has so much potential to get even better. At 21, he has age on his side and is already performing at such a high level for Leipzig and Norway this season.

Arsenal could do much worse by making a move for Nusa and giving their squad a lift it might need if they want to retain the Premier League title and go one better by winning the Champions League this season. And £66m is not a bad fee at all for a player that has the capabilities to be £100m-plus in years to come.

Nusa, who is renowned for his explosive pace and direct style, would slot in on the left side in a first-choice front three that includes Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka. Tzolis would then act as back-up with Eze following and supporting Martin Odegaard in the No.10.Some Arsenal fans have been calling for Odegaard to start ‘tapping up’ Nusa now, with the duo international teammates with Norway and have been playing together for some time now. That could offer the Gunners a real advantage in the race to sign him.After Norway's win against Wales, Odegaard was asked about the increasing interest involving teammate Nusa. But the Arsenal captain refused to be drawn into the speculation surrounding a potential move for the Leizpig talent.On the topic of future Arsenal players,Odegaard - during an interview with TV2 - was asked which one Norwegian player would be bring to north London if he had the option. “I can see you’re trying to get some big headlines here," Odegaard replied. “So no comment.”

Arsenal pursue a young, electric dribbler with six goals and seven assists as Andrea Berta ramps up talks.

#1282. Luke Graham seizes his chance to shine in Scotland back-line... now Stoke defender aims to make himself a fixture for years to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

This does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he said.

‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was announced as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream quickly become reality.

‘I’ve always said that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

‘He just said to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden

With the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ said Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham said. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of new, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season

Graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1280. Martin O'Neill Must Solve Celtic Left-Wing Problem After International Break

Martin O'Neill faces a difficult decision when Celtic return to action after the international break. The Bhoys went into the break with back-to-back wins, earning some relief from the heavy criticism they have received at times this season.

Going into the break, Celtic are four points clear at the top of the Premiership having played a game more, while they are in with a chance of progressing in the Europa League, now requiring six or seven points from their last four games.

There are some concerns about Celtic's playing style, there are bigger concerns about how the club is being run, but in terms of their actual season, Celtic are in far from a disastrous situation.

But it's going to be another interesting run of fixtures after the break, with Celtic having to deal with another condensed period due to their European participation. Due to poor recruitment in the summer, Celtic don't have many options in most positions, but that is not the case on the left side. O'Neill has the luxury of choosing between four players on the left, and there are particularly difficult decisions to make between three players.

Jota is now nearing full fitness, and while his first start in more than 18 months didn't go brilliantly, he has looked sharp in cameos, and he has the sort of quality that no one else in this squad can offer. The question is whether he can offer it consistently and stay fit in what is going to be a significant increase in load over the coming weeks.

Yang Hyun-jun will have something to say about the race to start on the left. The South Korean was excellent before going off for the Asian Games in early September. He then picked up a hamstring issue and didn't return until just before the break, but if he can get back to his early-season form, it will be hard not to choose Yang as the starter.

To make matters even more complicated for O'Neill, young Callum Osmand has dazzled on the left in recent weeks, producing some big performances, including a goal and an assist off the bench against Besiktas. Sebastian Tounekti is also an option on the left, but given his poor form this season and the competition on the left, the right-footed winger would be wise to try the right-side, where O'Neill is clearly less than satisfied with Haissem Hassan. Hassan was dropped from Celtic's whole matchday squad for their last game before the break.

But that left side is going to be a very difficult one to manage for O'Neill, who needs to balance the playing time between three very good players who will be battling for starts. Jota or Yang likely have the edge, and you have to wonder whether one of these left-wingers could do a job in the attacking midfield role, especially Callum Osmand. Celtic need better competition and an alternative to Benjamin Nygren, who needs to be kept on his toes amid a lack of consistency this season. That could be a solution to keep Osmand's confidence high amid recent positive performances, and he has shown what he can do centrally with creativity. Nygren doesn't do much defensively in any case, so there will be little lost by playing a striker there, with Osmand being a centre-forward by trade.

Celtic could be set for a key boost in the winter window if pieces fall into place to address former transfer shortcomings

#1279. Maccarone: ‘Italy focus only on victory in Belgium, Pio Esposito has great intelligence’

Roberto Mancini’s assistant Massimo Maccarone assures Italy will be ‘focused on only one result’ against Belgium this evening, and explains Pio Esposito has ‘great intelligence.’

It kicks off at the King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens on the Liveblog.

The hopes were not high when Mancini made his return to the Azzurri bench with a 2-0 home defeat to Belgium on September 25, prompting fears of relegation to Nations League B.

Instead, they are seven weeks later on top of their group, having earned a 1-1 draw in Paris and leapfrogged France thanks to a superior head-to-head record after Thursday’s 3-1 victory at San Siro.

A point this evening would suffice to secure a quarter-final place in the Nations League, but Italy have their sights set on top spot and revenge for their loss in Rome.

“The lads are accustomed to a certain style of game, they need to not think about getting two results out of three, but only on the one,” Maccarone told RAI Sport.

It is reported that Federico Dimarco won’t be bumped into a more advanced role, because Mancini saw that as a sign of being too defensive.

Maccarone is of course a former striker at Middlesbrough, so does he give Inter’s Francesco Pio Esposito some pointers?

“Pio Esposito is very humble and eager to learn, he always asks for notes on how his games went. I try to give advice, he accepts it eagerly, and when you see a player act like that, it is a sign of great intelligence.”

#1278. DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

In 2024, researchers found a new driver of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): it was a gene called ETS2 that is overactive in immune cells owing to a DNA variant that predisposes people to the condition1. This variant had previously confounded researchers because it lies in a ‘gene desert’ nowhere near protein-coding sequences.

That discovery had involved gene-editing and other sophisticated molecular-biology techniques, and it identified potential new IBD treatments. Now, researchers at Google DeepMind in London have replicated aspects of the finding using an artificial-intelligence model, and they have done this without lifting a pipette. Their model is called AlphaGenome 2.

“They’ve managed to figure out the answer in 30 minutes, and it took us a year and a half of experiments,” says James Lee, an immunologist and geneticist at the Francis Crick Institute in London, who led the 2024 study. “It’s reassuring from our perspective.”

The AlphaGenome 2 model, which was announced today, is an update to an AI tool that predicts the molecular effects that ‘non-coding’ DNA sequences have, such as on the expression of other genes. These sequences comprise 98% of the human genome, but they are among the hardest to decipher. The latest model makes these predictions in hundreds of mouse and human cell types.

Two months ago, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome Atlas: these were predictions for every possible single-letter DNA change to the human genome — a total of nine billion variants.

These and other predictions were made with a tool called AlphaGenome 1 and came with a major caveat: they did not specify the precise kind of cell — be it antibody-making B cells or pancreatic β-cells — in which a variant was likely to act. “Having something that cannot predict cell-type specificity is a bit of a problem, which is why it hasn’t been hugely useful for us,” says Lee.

But researchers know that many non-coding DNA sequences — including the variant that Lee’s team mapped, which is part of a sequence called a gene enhancer — tend to be active in specific types of cell.

“If you want to understand variants associated with genetic diseases, then you have to ask yourself what are the cell types that are affected,” says Žiga Avsec, a DeepMind researcher who leads the AlphaGenome team.

To develop an AI model that could decipher variant effects in diverse cells, Avsec’s team trained AlphaGenome 2 on single-cell gene activity and other measurements made in more than 100 million cells, across 68 tissues. AlphaGenome 1, by contrast, was fed data collected in ‘bulk’ samples of heterogeneous cells.

The result is a richer, more fine-grained representation of the differences between cells, says Adam Gayoso, a Google DeepMind scientist and co-author of a preprint describing the model on the company’s website.

AlphaGenome 2 also isn’t limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human cell and 311 kinds of mouse cell it was trained on. Researchers can provide the model with new single-cell gene-activity data — such as those from cells in a disease state — and generate gene-variant predictions. This could help researchers to identify variants underlying disease more quickly, says Gayoso.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03673-0

Stankey, C. T. et al. Nature 630, 447–456 (2024).
