#1277. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

EvertonOFF Johnson, Mykolenko ON Dibling, Hackney

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Big chance for Everton. White thinks he has time when he heads the ball back to Raya but he does not connect well and Barry is there to pick it up and he flicks a shot at goal but Raya reacts quickly to parry the ball.

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

The conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Chance for Arsenal. Rice finds space behind the Everton midfield and drives forward. He plays a pass to Lewis-Skelly, who lays it off to Eze. The England midfielder sidefoots a cross into the box but no one in an Arsenal shirt is there to meet it.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

#1276. 15 Players With the Greatest First Touch in Football History [Ranked]

There are a select few players in world football – past and present - that could give you a masterclass in perfecting a first touch and the likes of Dimitar Berbatov, Dennis Bergkamp and Ronaldinho are on hand to do so.

You can rack up as many goals, assists and trophies as you like, but without perfecting the basics – and in this particular case, your first touch – it’s all worthless. There’s an exclusive club, however, which includes those who have a penchant for plucking a ball out of thin air – like it was second nature.

It's one of the basics of becoming a professional at the highest level, but remember: not all footballers are that blessed. For aspiring youths, it is a staple part of the game that is sorely overlooked and one – that, if it can be perfected – will go a long way in terms of making a breakthrough.

But before you switch to YouTube and indulge in videos of first touch mastery, let's take a look at the top 15 first-touchers in the history of the beautiful game - ranked in order with the following ranking factors taken into consideration.

Commonly remembered as one of the most underrated performers in Premier League history thanks to the star-studded nature of Manchester City during his pomp, David Silva – nicknamed El Mago – was a magician. The Spaniard, while deceiving the opposition and sometimes even his teammates, made the difficult aspect of the beautiful game look so effortless.

That included his Velcro-like touch. Capable of plucking the ball from any height, the way the dainty playmaker wafted across the pitch was as tenacious as it was elegant – but it is the latter that makes him such a memorable asset of the English top flight and one of the greatest foreign players to ever play in it.

Former Manchester City winger Riyad Mahrez arguably possesses one of the best first touches in modern football and has most recently showcased his expertise in this department in the Middle East. No touch in his repertoire seemed to be the same, though all were done so acutely and with such poise.

What’s so special is his ability to set himself up in a sense that, in turn, could lead to a goal-scoring opportunity. There’s no doubt that his first touch was an attribute to thank for his long-term importance in Pep Guardiola’s teams. Now plying his trade in Qatar, there’s no doubt that his godly first touch has followed him. You never lose it, in truth.

A lot of football’s aspects come fairly simply to the towering Swede and a pinpoint first touch was one of them. With regard to being a focal point who is able to hold the ball up thanks to his pristine touch, you can end your pursuit now. Zlatan Ibrahimovic – at the peak of his powers – was the go-to guy.

Rasmus Hojlund has joined some illustrious company as Manchester United's newest number nine.

Whether it was a drilled ball on the floor and one rifled into his midriff, you’d be unwise to bet against the journeyman being able to control it and already looking for his next port of call, which would often be the overlapping wide men who had just played the pass.

The archetypal enganche, Juan Roman Riquelme encapsulated everything joyous about football: from the touch-tight dribbling to the careful eye for panache to the otherworldly imagination and, by the end of his career, was considered a Boca Juniors legend with just shy of 300 appearances under his belt. So much so that he now serves as the President of the Argentinian top flight outfit.

Even throughout the twilight period of his career when the Argentine’s physical abilities were declining, Riquelme – who was neither quick nor looking to cover every blade of glass – had to rely on his technical qualities, but that was seldom a problem like it was for other players. Cultured is the word.

Whether it was a short or a long pass, you could guarantee that Andres Iniesta would be able to keep it in close proximity. Watching from home, it may look easy, but that’s because he – alongside many others – made it look so, but for the majority of players, it would be a cause for concern.

Iniesta would always offer his teammates an outlet, whether he was in a sticky situation or not, and his sheer understanding of how football works attests to his unfailing first touch. A true orchestrator in the peak tiki-taka era at Barcelona, having a delightful touch was the first question asked at the interview stage.

Best known for forming a formidable partnership with Cristiano Ronaldo down the left flank during some of Real Madrid’s glory days, it would be remiss to disregard Marcelo’s first touch ability. It’s the stuff of dreams, in truth.

Virgil van Dijk, Franz Beckenbauer, and Rio Ferdinand all feature...

Talented enough to leave fans gawking in the wake of another first-class touch, the Brazilian often made the left side his own. Like it was the easiest thing in the world, he would often stop the ball dead when a ball was fizzed at him or whether a teammate played a cross-field ball. Despite not being a forward, the Los Blancos icon is up there with the very best in the game in terms of their first touch.

Whether it was scoring goals, going on a mazy run or producing a first touch from the gods, Diego Maradona captivated everything joyous about football. The diminutive Argentine embodied the art of composure and his fleet-footed nature made bringing down a ball like second nature. Just watch any video of the former Napoli ace juggling a ball and you’ll understand.

It was the type of thing that you could watch on loop – all without tiring. Hailed as one of the finest midfielders in the history of the sport, his control of the ball was unrivalled, and it was often followed by an extraordinary move. If his first touch didn’t leave you perplexed, what he did next certainly did.

The silky German certainly dazzled during his stint in England – that’s when he could be bothered, however. Likened to a wizard on his day, Mesut Ozil’s first few games for Arsenal made it apparent that the Premier League was about to be spellbound by his first touch ability. And once he departed for Fenerbahce eight years later, it was only then that people started to appreciate the true beauty of his play.

Since making his bow for Schalke 04 way back when, the first-touch wizardry from the playmaker has been a skill to behold. Ozil was, throughout his career, truly blessed with outstanding technique and has attributed this to a training regime which involved juggling with medicine balls. We know, mental!

In the Dutchman’s own words, he said: “Touching the ball is highest form of technique. But to touch it perfectly once, you need to have touched it 100,000 times in training!” And Johan Cruyff had certainly perfect the mastery of the first touch. Also the pioneer of the fabled ‘Cruyff Turn’, the glittering forward had a first touch of dreams – as evidenced by his influence on football and its philosophy.

Recognised as one of the greatest football players of all time, the Amsterdam-born phenom had no issues with turning players inside out on a regular basis and his close control was a pivotal factor in that.

Why do it normally when you can add in a bit of flair? Not only does Neymar have one of the best first touches in the game right now, but it’s the audacity in which he performs them that sees him so high on this list. One look at his highlight reel will leave you weak at the knees in awe.

Being able to bring the ball down so close-knit to his body is an invaluable trait to have, especially when sprucing into attacks at the speeds he and his teammates tend to do. It’s the reason defenders struggle to get the ball off him.

#1275. Van Bommel: ‘Belgium play good football first, but Italy underestimated’

Belgium coach Mark van Bommel explains his choices against Italy, warning the Azzurri are ‘underestimated’ even though he is no fan of their football. ‘The way they play basically doesn’t matter.’

It kicks off at the King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens on the Liveblog.

The Nazionale scenario seemed to be all doom and gloom after opening this Nations League group with a 2-0 home defeat to Belgium on September 25.

However, they have since surged to top spot by beating Turkiye twice, drawing 1-1 in Paris, then beating France 3-1 at San Siro on Thursday.

It means they need only a point here to be sure of qualification for the quarter-finals, and Belgium fully expect an old-school Italy defensive approach.

“I played in Italy myself, and if we won 1-0 there with very poor football, they were still on their feet to cheer us. That is the mentality,” former Milan midfielder Van Bommel told HLN.

“They have to win, but the way they do it basically doesn’t matter. We always want to play very good football. That’s where it starts for me, because then the chance of winning is greater if we play well first.”

However, when the Belgian media is too dismissive of the Italy squad, the coach does step in to give a warning.

“That dismisses Italy as a mediocre team. It is true they have missed three World Cup editions in a row, but historically, it is a great footballing nation. They really have a good squad, considering the development they have made since that first match.

“They are underestimated. We don’t need to be afraid, but they are not a bad opponent by any means.”

Romelu Lukaku missed the trip to Turkiye on Thursday, where they won 2-1, but the former Napoli striker is back on the bench tonight, as Atalanta forward Charles De Ketelaere keeps his place.

Is it because Big Rom can be used as a valuable boost off the bench?

“Lukaku has been doing that for quite some time, including before the World Cup. He decided many matches and scored goals,” added Van Bommel.

“Charles is doing very well. He is a modern striker. A big, strong, fast, and ball-holding striker, you see that more and more often. But that doesn’t mean Romelu couldn’t have started, mind you.”

#1274. Aston Villa's Must Address Full-Back Crisis Before Top 4 Bid is Crippled

Aston Villa have a significant problem brewing at full-back, and it could cost them a place in the top four this season. It hasn't been comfortable season for Unai Emery and his men so far, which was to be expected after the turnover we saw at Villa Park over the course of the summer transfer window.

Star men Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Emi Martinez all left the West-Midlands, and replacing them was always going to be difficult, while Amadou Onana suffered a season-ending injury in the summer, leaving a gap in midfield that had to be filled.

A rocky start followed, at least in the Premier League, with Villa currently 10th and five points off the top four, but they have faired better in the Champions League, winning three of their four games so far, and the only defeat in that competition came against Barcelona.

Villa won't be panicking about their Premier League campaign, and rightly so - they are just five points off fourth, and there is plenty of time remaining. But if they don't address a clear problem within their squad in the January transfer window, then their top four bid is likely to collapse.

Villa were dealt an injury scare on Saturday night, when star right-back Matty Cash suffered a concussion after a nasty clash, and he will now enter concussion protocol. Symptoms govern the return to play with that particular setback, meaning Cash will need to come through a staged return to training without any symptom flare-ups before he can be cleared to play.

At the very least, it will put next weekend's clash with Sunderland at risk, and Villa fans will need no reminding of the crisis Emery has emerging at full-back. Aaron Wan-Bissaka has been dealing with a hamstring issue over recent weeks, and while he is hoping to return soon, hamstrings can be troubling for pacey full-backs.

Even on the other side, Matteo Ruggeri is out until some time in December, leaving Villa with one left-back in Ian Maatsen. Two left-backs and two right-backs isn't sufficient for a club playing in the Premier League and Champions League, and at the very least, Villa could do with a full-back who can cover on either side for situations like the one that is developing - the same one that forced Taylor Harwood-Bellis to play out of position at right-back in the draw against Manchester United.

It's a situation that simply has to be addressed by Emery and the Villa board in the January transfer window. Injuries only rack up going into the festive period and beyond, and Villa have to be one step ahead. This Cash scare may be the wake-up call they need.

Aston Villa face Sunderland in their next game on Saturday - but Unai Emery could be without one key player ahead of the Villa Park clash

#1273. Juventus worry as Celik suffered injury in France vs. Turkiye warm-up

Juventus are concerned after Zeki Celik pulled out of tonight’s Nations League game between Turkiye and France due to a thigh injury, so that will need to be evaluated.

It kicks off in Bordeaux at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

They are in the same Nations League group as Italy, who are in turn visiting Belgium in Brussels this evening.

Celik had been named in the starting XI for Turkiye and was all ready to start until limping off during the warm-up.

A representative from the Turkish Football Federation confirmed to the media that Celik had felt a tightness in the back of his left thigh, so had withdrawn from the squad.

He has been replaced in the starting line-up by Baris Alper Yilmaz.

It is a blow not only for Turkiye, who are heading for relegation from Nations League A anyway after zero points from five games, but also for his club side Juventus.

The former Roma full-back had only just returned to the side from injury, so losing him again so quickly will prompt concern he suffered a relapse.

This will need to be evaluated when he is back in Turin after international duty.

#1272. Liverpools' Elliott Could Have Loan Spell Cancelled as Review Scheduled

Harvey Elliott's nightmare run continues, this time in Spain, and he could find himself back at Liverpool before he knows it. Elliott arrived at current loan club Valencia with a some excitement surrounding his arrival, with Los Ché having struggled in recent times and in need of some attacking flair.

But things are not going well for 23-year-old, and this time it has nothing to do with footballing administration. Elliott is said to have been put on a special fitness programme following his arrival due to weight concerns, and the Spanish giants are also said to have concerns over his professionalism.

It certainly didn't help when he recently came off the bench against rivals Villarreal and almost immediately got sent off for a double dissent offence. Elliott complained about a decision that had nothing to do with him, earning a yellow card, and after he reacted negatively, the referee sent him off. To make matters worse, Villarreal then went on to score a stoppage time winner. He hasn't played since, serving his suspension and then being left on the bench for the last game before the break.

According to La Provence, Valencia sporting chief Braulio Vázquez is reassessing recent signings to see who hasn't lived up to expectations, and as part of that review, he could decide to send Elliott back to Liverpool in January in order to redirect the wage contribution on more effective players. The main issue is that manager Javier Aguirre clearly isn't very impressed with Elliott, and the death stare he gave him after his red card was almost indescribable.

Although the former Mexico boss did offer some encouragement before the break, saying:

“We have been talking with him so that he improves in some things and I think he has done well in training.”

Of course, this situation comes after Elliott had a miserable season of last, frozen out by Villa due to a contractual issue, namely that Villa did not allow him to reach a certain number of games to avoid triggering an automatic purchase clause.

Elliott is struggling to find his way, and with only six league appearances and no league starts this season, it's clear his current spell is not going well. Liverpool need to find the creative star a good home, even if it means permanently, but it's also down to Elliott. You never know what the truth is with these situations within clubs, but it does appear as though he needs to knuckle down if he is to find a long-term home somewhere.

Dominik Szoboszlai has sparked fury among Liverpool supporters.

#1271. Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

It was a chastening afternoon for the champions who last won at Welford Road in January 2023.

Phil Dowson, Saints’ director of rugby, felt his side were in the contest at the interval but bemoaned the fact that they were unable to handle Leicester’s second-half power surge.

“It was a scrap. The conditions were going to dictate that. And they had some set-piece dominance which hurt us,” he said.

“That gave them a ton of energy and we didn’t seem able to respond, which was probably the most disappointing thing.

“In the second half we didn’t seem to have that same buzz about us.”

Dowson was reluctant to blame the tunnel flare-up for the turnaround.

“The fracas at the end of the half was just one of those things that happens in a derby – that happens every derby. I don’t think that’s necessarily something that triggered anything,” he said.

“It’s not as if anyone got filled in. Well, you just can’t anymore, can you? These games are going to be hostile and in the current game you can’t throw anything. It’s just push and shove and talk c--p, so I don’t think that had any impact.”

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#1270. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli urges Ben Gannon-Doak to improve his end product but insists he's happy with progress of mercurial winger

Published: 17:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ said the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden

‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is important he knows that.’

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – currently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ said Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

#1269. Extraordinary materials shaped by the principles of complex networks

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Marco Paggi is at the IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, 55100 Lucca, Italy.

Scientists’ knowledge of the connectivity, robustness and functionality of complex networks — such as those that describe interactions in chemical and biological systems, social relationships and the Internet — has increased enormously over the past few decades1. The foundations of modern complex-network science were established by the pioneering contributions of Albert-László Barabási and Réka Albert2,3, who revealed universal mechanisms that explain the emergence of highly non-uniform network configurations. Writing in Nature, Both et al.4 report that ideas from network science can be used to design materials that have remarkable mechanical properties, incorporating connection diversity and variable component sizes found in complex systems into materials engineering.

#1268. Spain vs England: What Happened to Spark Tunnel Bust-Up

The world champions Spain welcomed England to the Metropolitano for a UEFA Nations League group game on Sunday and tempers flared between the two sides.

Thomas Tuchel's men dominated the first half, pressing aggressively and affording the 2026 World Cup winners no time or space. Jude Bellingham came within inches of opening the scoring early on.

But Harry Kane netted his 94th England goal from the penalty spot shortly before half-time after the Bayern Munich forward was brought down inside the area. With the visitors leading 1-0 going into the break, a scuffle broke out just before the players reached the tunnel.

Clement Turpin blew the half-time whistle, but the players couldn't even reach the tunnel before things got out of hand. It appeared that England's Ben White and Spain's Fabian Ruiz were at the centre of the flare-up.

Almost everyone else quickly got involved, either to have their say in the disagreement or to act as peacemakers. Kane was seen asking the referee to step in. Watch the video below.

During ITV's half-time segment, presenter Mark Pougatch gave a small insight into what had happened. "You might have noticed as the players were coming off, Fabian Ruiz and Ben White were having a frank exchange of views."

Dele Alli is set to earn a huge £7.6 million payday despite not playing football for the last 19 months.

Ian Wright, on the punditry panel alongside Roy Keane, appeared delighted to see the passion in the game. The former England striker replied: "Nice one, Ben White. Yeah, good."

Footage from the stands showed the likes of Dan Burn and David Raya stepping in to keep the two men apart very quickly to prevent anything escalating. Marc Cucurella was among those looking to get involved.

One thing that didn't appear to get picked up originally was a brief squabble between midfielders Bellingham and Martin Zubimendi. The latter, who started the game for Spain, appeared to push a member of England's coaching staff.

Bellingham tried his best to get to Zubimendi, but there were too many bodies in the way. The 23-year-old still appeared to shout something in the Arsenal star's direction. Watch from another angle below.

Many people took to social media to point out the tension between Bellingham and Zubimendi, which ITV's commentary and punditry teams appeared to miss.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1267. Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

Kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

#1265. Vinicius Jr Named 3 Toughest Opponents He's Faced - Picked Two Englishmen

By combining exceptional technique, blistering pace and an eye for goal, there are few defenders that Real Madrid and Brazil star Vinicius Jr would be intimidated by – yet, throughout his career, the winger has singled out three particularly difficult opponents.

That's right, even a player as naturally gifted as the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up – who is regularly considered among the finest wingers in world football today – can occasionally find himself up against a challenging opponent, even if such occasions are relatively rare.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: In June 2024, Vinicius became the youngest player to score in two Champions League finals.

Vinicius has now enjoyed many seasons wearing the famous white shirt of Los Blancos, meaning he has come up against some of football's most formidable defenders. Interestingly enough, he named two Englishmen amongst his very toughest.

According to SPORT in 2023, the Brazilian international identified Ronald Araujo as the 'best defender' he had ever faced. The Barcelona star is now on loan at Liverpool, but clearly always gave Vini Jr a tough time when they met.

Speaking about the Uruguayan centre-back's impressive physical strength, Vinicius explained that Araujo's quality is precisely why he represents one of football's biggest clubs in Barcelona. As reported by The Sun, the winger stated:

The best defender I have ever faced is Araujo. He's very strong and very good. That's why he plays for Barca.

The two South Americans have shared numerous memorable battles, particularly during their regular El Clasico meetings – although their head-to-head record remains perfectly balanced, with six victories each.

Several players around the world have astronomically high release clauses which will never be matched by buying clubs.

Araujo joined the Catalan outfit in 2018 before making the step up to the first team in 2020. He then established himself as an integral member of the squad, recording more than 150 appearances for the club, before heading to Liverpool on loan in 2026/27.

Before naming Araujo, however, Vinicius had previously spoken highly of two current England internationals – Chelsea skipper Reece James and Manchester City icon Kyle Walker – during an interview with SPORTbible in 2022.

I've played against a lot of them and the most difficult opponents were Chelsea's [Reece] James and [Kyle] Walker, of Manchester City.

Looking at James first, the injury-hit Chelsea defender has faced the challenge of containing Vinicius on four separate occasions. Walker, meanwhile, has come out on top three times, although he has yet to find the net in any of their previous encounters.

Walker possesses the kind of explosive speed that can trouble even the most dangerous attackers in the game – something Vinicius has experienced on six occasions. #1264. John McGinn warns Tartan Army it might take 18 MONTHS for Scotland to click into gear under new boss Pocognoli

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:03 EST, 14 November 2026

Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.

Steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. It happened primarily because a limited squad was unable to outperform two top-ten nations in Brazil and Morocco who could call upon infinitely superior footballers.

Sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ said the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most important thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create big chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’

If that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’

Give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

The sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’

Even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli

‘We need to play slightly better,’ he said. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’

Friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

The brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

‘So, we had a wee chat and I think we both said the most important thing was just no matter who hit it, hit the back of the net.’

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high

Tomorrow, the equation is clear. To finish second in the Nations League group and secure a place in pot two for the Euro draw, Scotland must beat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t beat North Macedonia.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

‘Difficult,’ said McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’

#1261. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he said.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”

Brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions.
